notes: NFR-12: every Decision Layer parameter lives here, never in code, so any historical
backtest result can be reproduced exactly from its parameter set.
STATUS = placeholder. Every value below is a Design-§6 default, NOT a fitted value.
Nothing here has seen data yet. The fitting schedule is:
market_shrinkage.w      <- Phase 5 checkpoint (the project's truth serum)
Code must refuse to emit live recommendations while status == 'placeholder'.
PHASE C, 2026-08-24: the w checkpoint and the selection rule are separate
gates and BOTH are still shut. w fits at 0.000 (data/w_checkpoint.json), and
no sharp reference available in the live feed clears the >=2-season bar

2026-08-27: status moved placeholder -> experimental so the Pinnacle-referenced rule can run live. NOT 'fitted': the rule has five seasons of evidence, the 25-book panel it now runs on has none, and selection_rule.blocked_by says so on every response.

market_shrinkage.comment: Fitted at the Phase 5 checkpoint and the fitted value is 0.000 (data/w_checkpoint.json). w_fitted=true records that the estimate was MADE, not that it was positive; p_used is therefore q_fair and every surviving pound of expected value is price, not model. Requirements 8.4 calls a w near zero a valid and publishable finding, and this is it.

benchmark.comment: DECIDED: the de-vigged consensus closing price (AvgC*) is the primary market benchmark. That confines the headline comparison to 2019/20 onward, because consensus closing columns do not exist before then — verified against the live archive, not assumed from Requirements §7.3. Pinnacle's own closing price reaches back to 2012/13 and is retained as a SECONDARY, single-book benchmark for calibration and RPS work over a longer horizon; it is never mixed into the primary number. 2025/26 sits after the Pinnacle regime break and is held entirely separate rather than pooled (Requirements §7.3). holdout_season is the NFR-10 untouched season: the last pre-break season, so it shares a regime with the training window.

devig.comment: FR-28. Selected per competition by log-loss and calibration error against realised outcomes, and rewritten by scripts/select_devig_method.py. A competition keeps the Shin default unless another method wins SIGNIFICANTLY on a paired per-match test; a merely higher-ranked method is not enough. Default is Shin rather than proportional because proportional de-vig systematically overstates longshot fair probability and would manufacture phantom value on draws and away underdogs (Design §6.2). Re-fitted 2026-09-04 across eight leagues: POR.PRIMEIRA and TUR.SUPERLIG are the ONLY two competitions where the choice is significant (power over shin, p=0.004 and p=0.009). That is consistent rather than surprising — both carry a fatter book margin (5.9% and 6.3% against England's 4.5%), and the three methods only diverge materially when there is more vig to remove.

grading.comment: Design §6.4. c_edge is deliberately NON-monotonic: exp(-((edge_prob - e_peak)/sigma)^2), with an automatic F above e_ceiling. An apparent 20-point edge in a market this efficient almost always means the model is blind to something, not that the market is wrong.

guardrails.comment: FR-33. Evaluated BEFORE grading; each firing forces grade F with a logged reason. odds_coverage=false is also a guardrail and is enforced from the taxonomy, not from this file.

staking.comment: Design §6.5. lambda defaults to 0.25; the backtest publishes the full growth-vs-drawdown frontier rather than asserting one value. Caps are fractions of bankroll.

market_engine.comment: Design §6.1 / §11. matrix_max_goals is the truncation point deferred from Design §11; the matrix is renormalised after truncation and Phase 3 asserts it sums to ~1.

reporting.comment: The CLV label is mandatory and literal (Design §6.6): football-data.co.uk's base snapshot is Friday afternoon, not a true opening line, so measured movement understates what an early bettor could capture. min_cell_sample_size greys out edge-map cells rather than displaying noise as signal (Design §6.8).

odds_regime.comment: Requirements §7.3. Pinnacle was dropped from Max/Avg on this date. Pooling the two regimes without adjustment is a correctness bug, so the default forbids it.

comment: ACTIVE, and experimental rather than fitted. The distinction is the point:
`fitted` would claim the parameters below were estimated to the project's own
standard, and they are not — see blocked_by.
reference = Pinnacle. MODEL_CARD 5 measures +0.51% Friday-to-close CLV at
t=+7.53 clustered over five pre-break seasons and 7,790 matches on
Pinnacle-referenced selections. Phase C could not run it forward because the
free fixture feed does not publish Pinnacle; The Odds API does, so it can.
market_families = 1x2 ONLY, and this is not a simplification. MODEL_CARD 4
measured picking the largest apparent edge ACROSS markets at -2.12% ROI
against +0.13% for committing to one market in advance, because maximum-edge
selection finds the model's own largest errors. A daily pick ranked across
all 86 selections would be exactly that failure.
The rule gates STAKING, not only ranking: a selection the evidence does not
cover is not a bet however well it grades.

blocked_by.what_is_still_unproven: The +0.51% was measured against football-data.co.uk's Max column over a 7-30 book panel. Live, the best quote comes from a 25-book Odds API panel — a different estimator, so the rule's calibration is inherited rather than re-measured. Requirements line 250's >=2-season bar is met for the RULE and not for this PANEL.
blocked_by.consequence: Every selection is emitted with config_status=experimental and the evidence attached. Treat the output as a live test of a measured rule on a new price panel, not as a validated edge.
blocked_by.clears_when: The captured live_odds series reaches two seasons and scripts/study_selection_rules.py reproduces the result on this panel.

not_used_and_why.odds_max_as_reference: Selecting on the max-vs-consensus spread and then scoring the max price's movement scores a variable on itself. Measured: the spread narrows from +11.64% to +10.23% on selected rows while the consensus moves 0.28% AGAINST the bet. Regression to the mean, not edge.
not_used_and_why.odds_b365: No pre-break signal (-0.07%, t=-1.09) despite being in the feed.

comment: A PRODUCT requirement, not a measured one, and the two must never be
confused in the output. When no selection clears the Pinnacle rule on a
day that has football, the single highest-confidence selection is
surfaced so the day is never blank.
'Confidence' is p_model: the selection this project's own model is most
certain about. That is NOT the rule's quantity. The rule asks whether a
price is wrong; this asks which outcome is most likely, and a heavy
favourite at a fair price is highly confident and worth nothing.
MODEL_CARD 4 measured selection of this shape at -2.12% ROI against
+0.13% for committing to one market. Every such row therefore carries
selection_basis='confidence', is sized at a FLAT stake rather than by
Kelly -- Kelly sizes from an edge and there is no measured edge here, so
sizing from one would be inventing a number -- and is recorded
separately in the ledger so its CLV can be measured apart from the
rule's. That separation is what turns this from a guess into an
experiment that answers itself in a few months.

selection_rule.competitions_comment: The competitions where the rule has been MEASURED to earn, not the competitions that have odds. Same argument as market_families, along the other axis: the pooled CLV figure is an average, and an average is what hides a competition the rule does not work in. Measured per competition on the pre-break window with the holdout excluded (data/selection_rule_study.json -> per_competition); a competition is listed only if it has >=2 seasons, positive mean CLV and clustered t > 2. EXCLUDED and why: NED.EREDIVISIE at -0.22% CLV, t=-0.82 over 5 seasons — a NEGATIVE point estimate, which the five Big-5 leagues were carrying to a comfortable pooled +0.43%. POR.PRIMEIRA at +0.27%, t=1.07 — positive but not resolvable at ~974 selections, so it is unproven rather than disproven, and it stays out until it is one or the other. TUR.SUPERLIG is IN at +0.47%, t=2.63. An empty list means unscoped and everything is eligible, which is how a config written before this field keeps working.
